The image shows a sugarcane leaf with fine, elongated streaks running parallel to the leaf veins. The streaks are pale/light green to yellowish in color against a darker green background, creating a mosaic-like or streaked pattern along the length of the leaf. The pattern is linear and follows the vascular tissue of the leaf.

This pattern — fine, parallel, vein-aligned streaks giving a streaked/mosaic appearance — is characteristic of **Streak Mosaic** caused by Sugarcane streak mosaic virus (SCSMV). This is distinct from Sugarcane Mosaic Virus (SCMV), which typically shows more irregular mosaic patches. The fine, continuous streaking along veins is the hallmark of SCSMV streak mosaic disease.
